bib.title: Retrieval-Pretrained Transformer: Long-range Language Modeling with Self-retrieval
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 21 Jul 2024); the PDF names no venue

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; appendices A-C (implementation, CCA complexity, DPR training) not read in detail

question: Can a retriever be trained jointly with the LM from scratch, as a native part of it, and does a semantic training signal beat a lexical one?
hypothesis: Computing retrieval queries from the LM's own hidden states and training the retriever to pick chunks that raise the next chunk's probability under a reference LM gives better perplexity than a fixed BM25 retriever or lexical supervision.
contributions: Self-retrieval: retriever inputs come from the lower decoder layers; retrieved chunks are fused by chunked cross-attention (CCA) in the upper layers
A retriever loss (LambdaRank) whose ranking comes from a reference scoring LM, not lexical overlap
Neighbor gating and scheduled sampling to make training stable
Perplexity and retrieval-metric gains on four long-document datasets

method.summary: Split each document into 64-token chunks; for each chunk retrieve K earlier chunks of the same document with a learned bilinear score over pooled lower-decoder states; fuse them with RETRO-style CCA. Supervision: BM25 gives 20 candidates per chunk, a frozen Pythia 1.4B scores log P(next chunk | candidate) / P(next chunk | two preceding chunks), positives are those with score above 0, LambdaRank trains the retriever alongside the LM loss.

datasets.name: ArXiv, CodeParrot, PG19, Books3
datasets.size: train tokens in millions: ArXiv 12,000; CodeParrot 5,000; PG19 3,000; Books3 25,000; median document length 16,368 / 29,269 / 82,659 / 113,496 tokens (Table 1)
datasets.preprocessing: CodeParrot files from one repository concatenated

models.name: RPT-Sem
models.architecture: 12 layers, hidden 1024, 8 heads; upper half uses CCA with 2 neighbours

training.objective: LM loss + alpha_ret * LambdaRank retriever loss
training.regularisation: scheduled sampling of gold neighbours, annealed 1 to 0 over first 90% of training

inference.retrieval: Faiss index on CPU over lower-decoder keys of all earlier tokens of the document; top-K by dot product

metrics.name: Precision@2, Recall@10, nDCG@20
metrics.definition: against positives defined by the scoring LM's target score

results.claim: RPT-Sem reaches test perplexity 2.77 / 2.17 / 10.96 / 13.91 on ArXiv / CodeParrot / PG19 / Books3, against 3.11 / 2.30 / 11.48 / 15.00 for the Transformer-XL baseline and 2.94 / 2.17 / 11.44 / 14.60 for RETRO with BM25.
results.note: on CodeParrot RPT-Sem ties RETRO at 2.17

results.claim: A semantic training signal beats a lexical one: RPT-Lex gets 2.92 / 2.23 / 11.59 / 14.32 versus RPT-Sem 2.77 / 2.17 / 10.96 / 13.91; on retrieval, average Precision@2 is 25.2% BM25, 23.2% RPT-Lex, 30.0% RPT-Sem.
results.setup: four datasets, positives defined by the scoring LM

results.claim: Joint training matters: swapping the retriever RPT-Sem was trained with for a separately trained DPR-style retriever worsens every dataset (for example Books3 13.91 to 14.66, ArXiv 2.77 to 2.98).
results.setup: DPR-style retriever trained per dataset with the standard DPR procedure
results.note: the authors read this as retriever and LM coordinating

results.claim: Ablations: removing neighbor gating raises Books3 perplexity from 13.91 to 18.68; no teacher forcing raises PG19 from 10.96 to 13.10.

An oracle that picks the best neighbours per the scoring LM improves RPT-Sem on Books3 from 13.87 to 12.74 and PG19 from 10.92 to 10.26 (3 neighbours baseline column as printed in the text), so retriever quality still limits the model.
results.note: the text compares against the 3-neighbour row

results.claim: RPT-Sem is slower to train than the Transformer-XL baseline: 1.51x time per update, against 1.35x for RETRO with BM25.
Retrieval helps even when the retrieved chunk is not a gold one, though gold retrievals give larger gains.
results.quote: we witness improvements even in cases where a gold chunk was not retrieved

limits: Retrieval is only over earlier chunks of the same document, so the index is the context itself; it does not show retrieval from a web-scale corpus (the authors name scaling and corpus construction as open).
Models are small (242M parameters, 65B tokens) and compared with the authors' own implementations; single runs, no confidence intervals.
Perplexity is the main metric; no downstream task or factuality result.
Supervision only re-ranks the top-20 BM25 candidates, so retrieval quality is capped by BM25 recall (Fig 5).
Training costs 1.51x per update and a frozen scoring LM is needed.
